title: Polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille Bounds and Hardy--Littlewood Inequalities for Finite Local Systems
summary: The complex polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille inequality states that, for a $d$-homogeneous polynomial $P:\mathbb C^N\to\mathbb C$, $P(z)=\sum_{|α|=d}c_αz^α$, the coefficient norm $(\sum_{|α|=d}|c_α|^{p_d})^{1/p_d}$ is bounded by $B_d^{\mathrm{pol}}\|P\|_\infty$, where $p_d=2d/(d+1)$ and $B_d^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is independent of $N$. Here $\|P\|_\infty$ is the supremum norm on the unit polydisc. This inequality has a Boolean analogue for the Fourier--Walsh coefficients of functions of degree at most $d$, with the supremum taken over $\{-1,1\}^N$.
